summary: End-to-end ML platforms handle the full lifecycle—data prep, distributed training, fine-tuning, experiment tracking, model registry, deployment, and monitoring—at a scale that raw model APIs cannot. You need one when you're training or fine-tuning custom models, managing many experiments and models in production, or require governance, reproducibility, and MLOps controls; if you just need inference from a foundation model, a hosted model API is cheaper and simpler. The market is dominated by the three hyperscaler platforms (SageMaker, Vertex AI/now folded into Google's Gemini Enterprise stack, Azure ML) plus Databricks, with specialized AutoML and MLOps tooling clustering below.

platforms.name: AWS SageMaker (SageMaker AI)
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per compute instance-hour for training, inference, notebooks, and storage; no upfront fee. Savings plans available.
platforms.best_for: Teams already on AWS wanting a deeply integrated, service-oriented, full-lifecycle ML platform.

platforms.name: Azure Machine Learning
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go on underlying Azure compute/storage; no separate platform fee. Enterprise agreements and reserved instances available.
platforms.best_for: Enterprises standardized on Azure and Microsoft tooling needing strong governance and responsible-AI features.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per node-hour for training/prediction plus per-token pricing for foundation models; no platform subscription.
platforms.best_for: GCP-centric teams and those wanting tight integration with Gemini and Google data services (note: increasingly bundled into Gemini Enterprise as of 2026).

platforms.name: Databricks (MLflow + Mosaic AI)
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based DBU pricing on top of cloud compute; tiered by workload. Commit contracts available.
platforms.best_for: Organizations wanting a unified, multi-cloud lakehouse plus ML/LLMOps with strong data governance.

platforms.name: Weights & Biases
platforms.pricing: Free for personal/open-source; usage- and seat-based paid tiers; enterprise self-hosted licensing.
platforms.best_for: ML research and engineering teams needing best-in-class experiment tracking and reproducibility across any training stack.

platforms.name: MLflow
platforms.pricing: Free open source; managed versions available via Databricks and cloud vendors.
platforms.best_for: Teams wanting a vendor-neutral, open-source standard for experiment tracking and model lifecycle management.

platforms.name: DataRobot
platforms.pricing: Enterprise subscription / contract-based; custom quotes (no public pay-as-you-go).
platforms.best_for: Enterprises and less-technical analysts wanting automated, governed ML with minimal hand-coding.

platforms.name: H2O.ai
platforms.pricing: Open-source core free; enterprise (Driverless AI, H2O AI Cloud) via subscription/contract.
platforms.best_for: Data science teams wanting open-source-rooted AutoML with strong explainability and flexible deployment.

platforms.name: Modal
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-second serverless compute (CPU/GPU); free monthly credits; no idle cost.
platforms.best_for: Engineers wanting code-first, serverless GPU for training and deploying models without managing infrastructure.

platforms.name: Kubeflow
platforms.pricing: Free open source; pay only for underlying Kubernetes infrastructure.
platforms.best_for: Platform teams wanting a portable, Kubernetes-native MLOps stack with no vendor lock-in.

platforms.name: Hugging Face (Hub + Inference Endpoints + AutoTrain)
platforms.pricing: Free tier; pay-as-you-go inference endpoints and compute; Enterprise Hub subscription.
platforms.best_for: Teams building on open-source transformers/LLMs needing a shared hub plus easy fine-tuning and deployment.
